gaps: media or analyst material is present and ranks below issuer sources

mechanism: Mid-market operators pay a recurring per-seat fee to keep their scheduling and payroll in one system, and they keep paying because the payroll record lives in it.

key_variables.why_it_decides: Revenue is per-seat, so seats decide growth more than pricing does.

key_variables.variable: Gross logo churn among sub-100-seat customers
key_variables.why_it_decides: The smallest cohort churns first and sets the floor on net retention.
Attach is what turns a schedule tool into a system of record and lifts switching cost.
The story only works if collected cash follows booked revenue.

checks.finding: Recurring subscription revenue with disclosed seat counts and a stated retention figure in the latest filing.
Switching cost is real but shallow; the filing names three competitors offering migration credits.
No restatement, no auditor change, related-party note is limited to a disclosed lease.
Trades above its own three-year multiple range on structured data; expensive, not unintelligible.
Diluted share count up about 1% year over year, consistent with disclosed SBC.
Net cash position covers more than two years of the current burn rate at the reported cash figure.

vetoes.finding: No enforcement action or restatement in the filing history reviewed.
Per-seat subscription pricing is stated in the filing.
Operating cash flow positive in each of the four reported periods.
Share growth is roughly 1% against double-digit revenue growth.

mirror_test: It sells one subscription that mid-market operators use to schedule staff and run payroll.
It earns because the payroll record of employment lives inside the product and moving it is disruptive.
For the position to work, seat growth has to stay positive while the smallest customers keep renewing.
It breaks if a competitor's migration credit makes switching cheap enough that the payroll record stops being sticky.
If that happens the position is exited rather than averaged down, because the entire thesis was the switching cost.

evidence.summary: Latest quarterly filing: revenue recognition policy, seat disclosure, competitor discussion, related-party lease note.
Structured four-period series for revenue, net income, operating cash flow, cash and diluted shares.
Trade press reports a competitor offering migration credits; read as context, not as a filing fact.
